claims.statement: The dual-engine WebDAV bridge described by ADR-0156 D1 and the backup spec (a Java core plus a WebView `WebDavPlugin` and a Lynx `PictelioWebDavModule`) is historical: the WebView client package was deleted, and the only live bridge is `NativeModules.PictelioWebDav` → `PictelioWebDavModule` → `WebDavClient`/`BackupCrypto`, consumed by app-lynx's `utils/webDavBridge.ts`.

`stores/settingsStore.ts` is the single registry of persisted keys for app-lynx: it declares every key as a module constant and exports `BACKUP_DEVICE_KEYS`, `backupAccountKeys(uid)` and `BACKUP_IDB_KEYS`; source-scanning tests require every `*_KEY` literal to appear in `BACKUP_DEVICE_KEYS` and every entry to have a matching `applyRawKey` branch, so an unregistered key silently falls out of the backup domain.

`prefs()` is the single storage seam exported from settingsStore: in native mode it wraps `NativeModules.PictelioPrefs` (SharedPreferences file `CapacitorStorage`), and in web-core dev it uses the IndexedDB KV adapter; other stores must reuse it instead of hand-rolling a native/dev split.

Account-scoped settings are uid-suffixed keys read and written only when a uid is known: `loadSettings()` runs after `restoreToken()`, loads all device-scoped keys first regardless of login, then with no uid resets account refs to defaults and writes nothing, otherwise reads `show_r18_${uid}`, `show_r18g_${uid}`, `ai_filter_mode_${uid}`, `mute_tags_${uid}` and the two translate-consent keys.

Legacy account-key migration is idempotent and ordered: if the account key exists it returns, if the legacy key is absent it returns, otherwise it seeds the new key and only then removes the legacy key; the legacy set is environment-dependent (native `show_r18`/`show_r18g`, web-core dev `settings_show_r18`/`settings_show_r18g`).

On logout a `watch(currentUser, …, { flush: "sync" })` immediately resets the account-scoped refs to their defaults, and every account-scoped setter early-returns without persisting when no uid resolves, which is what prevents one account's switch state leaking into another session.

Keystore-backed secure storage is the only home for secrets: `SecureStorageCompat` uses AES/GCM/NoPadding with one AndroidKeyStore AES key per storage key (alias = `capacitor-storage_` + key), stores ciphertext in the `WSSecureStorageSharedPreferences` file as `Base64(ciphertext) + "\u0010" + Base64(iv)`, and backs `refresh_token`, `webdav_password` and `webdav_backup_password` via `NativeModules.PictelioSecureStorage` (IndexedDB in the dev preview).

WebDAV credential isolation is pinned by contract test: the two password keys `webdav_password` and `webdav_backup_password` must not be declared in `settingsStore` (only non-sensitive connection configuration enters the backup domain) and the credentials module must read and write through `PictelioSecureStorage`, not ordinary preferences.

The persisted-format strings `CapacitorStorage` (SharedPreferences file), `WSSecureStorageSharedPreferences` and the key prefix `capacitor-storage_` are frozen and must not be renamed, because renaming them orphans every installed user's stored settings and refresh token.

`PictelioPrefsModule` returns `""` for a missing key (never null, because the Lynx callback implementation crashes on null arguments) and Lynx JSON-quotes string callback arguments, so the JS preferences adapter runs every value through `unquoteNativeString` before use.

`utils/idbKV.ts` opens the `pictelio_lynx` IndexedDB at version 3 with the `kv` and `translations` object stores, creating every store under one version and converting `onblocked` into an explicit rejection so an upgrade can never hang silently.

The IndexedDB layer is a dev-preview and cache store, not a production one: on native PrimJS `indexedDB` is undefined, `idbGet`/`idbRemove` swallow the failure, and `idbSet` rejects — so the two keys read and written directly through idbKV (`settings_ugoira_mode`, `settings_detail_quality`) never persist on device and are absent from native snapshots.

Settings loading never trusts stored values: each key is validated against its own domain (enumerations, `"true"`/`"false"`, numeric ranges, JSON shape) and an illegal or unreadable value keeps the default and logs a warning, while setters update the in-memory ref and report write failures through `.catch(warn)` rather than swallowing them.

The restore rollback affordance rests on a single idbKV key: `savePreRestoreSnapshot` writes `webdav_pre_restore_snapshot` through `idbSet`, `applyPreparedRestore` awaits that hook before any write-back, and `undoLastRestore` replays the same key — so because the path requires `indexedDB`, its behaviour on native PrimJS is unverified.

The v1 snapshot envelope is a fixed nine-field object (`format: "pictelio-backup"`, `schemaVersion: 1`, `appVersion`, `engine`, `createdAt`, `excludedKeys`, `deviceKeys`, `accountKeys`, `sets`) whose values are the raw storage strings, and parsing refuses a file in three distinct ways — `NOT_BACKUP` for a wrong/missing format, `SCHEMA_TOO_NEW` only when the version exceeds the supported one, and `CORRUPT` for a missing, non-numeric or malformed field set.

Restore uses merge-by-keys: only keys present in the snapshot are planned for write-back (locally-added keys are untouched), account-scoped keys are applied only when their uid suffix matches the logged-in uid, snapshot `excludedKeys` are never written, and the write-back runs through the store's own setters so values are validated identically and unknown or foreign-account keys are reported as skipped.

Restore is deliberately two-phase — `prepareRestore` downloads, decrypts, parses and builds the plan plus the user-facing summary without writing anything, and `applyPreparedRestore` performs the write-back only after confirmation; on app-lynx the plan's `sets` are ignored because the client has no block/report store.

The backup pipeline is: collect the raw values (device keys plus current-account keys, with the runtime key `settings_webdav_last_backup` stripped and `sets` always empty) → build and serialize the snapshot → optionally encrypt on the Java side → `ensureDir` (MKCOL, 409 success) → `uploadWithVerify` → `prune` → stamp the last-backup time and clear the pre-restore snapshot.

Write-after-upload verification compares the remote `getcontentlength` (PROPFIND Depth 0) with the local byte count and falls back to a full GET byte comparison when the server omits the field; only `NETWORK` and `SERVER` failures are retried, other classified errors propagate immediately, and rotation keeps the newest 10 candidates by filename with delete failures logged but non-blocking.

The two fixed pipeline values — 3 write-verify attempts and 10 retained snapshots — have a single Java source of truth (`WebDavClient.VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` / `KEEP_BACKUPS`) mirrored by app-lynx constants, and a contract test asserts both sides equal the spec's literals.

Snapshot encryption is implemented only in Java and is self-describing: `PICTELIO-ENC1` magic (13 bytes) + salt (16) + iv (12) + AES-256-GCM ciphertext with the key derived by PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600 000 iterations, so the TS layer passes plain bytes plus the password and never implements crypto; a wrong password or corrupt file both surface as the `CRYPTO` kind ("password wrong or file corrupt").

Error handling across the bridge is a closed vocabulary: the UI renders eight kinds from `WEBDAV_ERROR_MESSAGES` (`CRYPTO` is added by the bridge while the Java `Kind` enum has the other seven), an unrecognised kind is downgraded to `SERVER` with a warning, and every bridge callback uses the two-argument `(code, payload)` shape because null callback arguments crash the Lynx runtime.

Startup auto backup hangs off the application lifecycle only: `initRouter()` calls `runStartupAutoBackup()` after `loadSettings()`, a disabled master switch means no IO at all, a never-back-up or unparseable timestamp runs the backup (with a warning for the corrupt stamp), elapsed ≤ N days skips, and any failure only warns without blocking startup.

The backup domain is a whitelist plus account keys, and device facts and rebuildable data are kept out of it: browsing-history, continue-reading, watch-later, search-history, engine device-fact keys, usage metrics and notification read-time keys are not exported and cannot be restored, which is asserted behaviourally for several of them.

The WebDAV configuration surface is exactly eight `settings_webdav_*` keys whose defaults are a blank URL/username, directory `Pictelio/backup` and an auto-backup period of 7 days; the Me page renders the block only on native (never in the web-core preview) and shows a non-HTTPS warning when the URL is not https.

`utils/webdavCredentials.ts` returns the raw value from the native secure-storage callback without the `unquoteNativeString` step that every other Lynx string-callback consumer applies, so whether a stored WebDAV password arrives JSON-quoted (and would then be sent verbatim as the Basic-auth credential) has no test or device evidence behind it.

The device-level end-to-end gate covers the backup upload path only: it seeds the WebDAV preferences, lets the startup hook run, and asserts a new snapshot with `engine: "lynx"` and a real build-injected `appVersion` plus the `settings_webdav_last_backup` write-back into real SharedPreferences; the restore path is not exercised there.

`mute_tags_${uid}` is collected into the snapshot through `backupAccountKeys` but classified as a device key on export, because `backupCore`'s `ACCOUNT_KEY_PREFIXES` covers only `show_r18_`, `show_r18g_` and `ai_filter_mode_`; write-back remains uid-gated because `applyRawKey` matches only `mute_tags_${current uid}`.
